title: Runtime: the command line, the processes and the lab folder
tagline: One command line, a handful of cooperating processes, talking through files and a pipe
summary: Everything starts as `python -m gamelab <command>` (gamelab/__main__.py). A few commands are long-lived processes: the elevated key player, the always-on perception service, a hunting command, the pet feeder with its guard, the mini-map's web server; an external babysitter script keeps the always-on ones running. They never call each other: they talk through files under `gamelab/lab/` (plans in an inbox, results in an outbox, flag files such as `STOP` and `ALARM.json`), a named pipe with shared memory for perception, and JSON-lines telemetry.
details_md:
**Why it is several processes, not one program.** Three facts of the PC shape the runtime:

- **Administrator rights.** MapleStory runs as administrator, and Windows blocks key presses from normal programs into admin windows. So exactly one small process, the **key player**, runs elevated (one click on Windows' UAC prompt, the "allow this app to make changes" dialog, per session), and everything else runs as a normal user and hands it *plans* (JSON data, never code) through files. The player loads as little of gamelab as it can: `tests/test_architecture.py` starts it the way the command line does and fails if any of the stack (behavior, motion, localization, attack, ui, sim, the game data, tkinter or gamelab's C pieces) comes along.
- **Python's global lock.** Planning holds the GIL; a perception thread in the same process got 16 of its 60 looks in 2 s while the planner worked. So perception runs in a process of its own. Until 2026-10-25 each command spawned a *feed child* of its own; since then one shared **perception service** (`python -m gamelab perceive`) looks at the game 15 times a second for everyone (the user: "run one shared perception process at all times").
- **Screen captures are scarce.** With `watch`, the pet feeder and a hunt each holding a DXGI desktop duplication (Windows' fast screen-capture interface), a third one failed (0x887A0022). Now no command captures the game for its looks: only the service builds `ScreenFrames` (`tests/test_architecture.py` checks it) and the commands read its frames. The exceptions are deliberate: the key player records the client area when a plan asks for frames (`snap`, `act`, `calibrate`, the recorded tests), `spot` and the old `gamelab recorder` grab with mss, and `bench-capture` and `bench-look --live` make their own grabber to time captures.

**Who runs.**

| Process | Started by | Elevated | Lives |
|---|---|---|---|
| key player (`player --elevate`) | a person (UAC) | yes | until `lab/STOP`, 24 idle hours, or a Lie Detector dealt with |
| perception service (`perceive`) | the babysitter, or any command's client (`service.ensure`, through WMI) | no | always; one per PC (a named mutex) |
| a hunting command (`tour --loop`, `hunt clear`, `nav`, `probe run`) | a person (or an external grind loop) | no | its run |
| pet feeder and guard (`pet --every 1`) | the babysitter, while no hunt runs | no | between hunts |
| parker (`nav --park`) | the guard, `gamelab stop`, or a person | no | one trip |
| mini-map / web page (`minimap`, `web`) | a person | no | until closed |
| children of the service | the service | no | the mini-game tracker while the alarm is up; a part writer per save |

The **babysitter** is a PowerShell script outside the repo (`babysit3.ps1` in `D:/MapleHelper-scratch`), polling every 5 s: it starts the service when none runs, stops the pet feeder while a hunting command's process is seen and starts it again after, and hands the rolling recording from an old `gamelab recorder` to the service.

**How they talk.** Nothing calls across processes directly. They talk through:

- **Files in `gamelab/lab/`**, written whole (a `.tmp` then a rename) and polled: the player's `inbox/` and `outbox/` (polled every 10 ms on both sides), flag files (`STOP`, `ALARM.json`, `stop_hunt.json`, `guard_mode.txt`), small state files that survive restarts (`hunt.json`, `parked.json`, `park_note.json`, `guard.json`, `pet.json`, `vitals.json`, `window_tries.json`, `alarm_keys.json`), and the recorder's own `recorder/inbox`, `outbox` and `status.json`.
- **A named pipe and shared memory** for perception: `\\.\pipe\gamelab-perceive` (its authkey and pid in `lab/perceive.json`), states pickled down it by a writer thread per client, the frames in rings of shared memory (16 look frames, 2 full-size).
- **Detached starts through WMI** (Windows Management Instrumentation): a process created through it is not its starter's child, so it outlives it (and gets none of its environment). `service.ensure` starts the service this way, the guard its park (`nav --park --tell`), and the babysitter everything it starts.
- **Named mutexes** (Windows' system-wide locks) for "one at a time": `Local\gamelab-perceive` and `Local\gamelab-rolling-recorder`.
- **stdin/stdout pipes** to the service's two kinds of child process (pickled messages down, replies up).
- **Telemetry**: JSON lines in `lab/telemetry/<time>-<command>.jsonl`, which the mini-map and the offline analyses read.

**The gates at the command line.** `main` decides who plays (`--character`, set before her physics loads), refuses a magician's `lock`, `combo` and `probe run`, and refuses the commands that bring the game forward or send input (`GAME_COMMANDS`, and `probe run`) while `lab/ALARM.json` is up; `keys --read` and `stats --read` check the alarm themselves and send nothing, `pet` goes on with its food only (the player takes it), and `perceive` and `watch` keep looking. The exit code tells a caller what happened: 0 done, 1 an error, 2 refused, 3 the Lie Detector, 4 the safety stop (also HP not read, a map too strong), 5 out of darts, 6 the key check, 7 the stat window, 8 out of MP, 9 a stop asked by `gamelab stop`. Whatever happens, `_close_perception` detaches the command from the service and prints what it had of it, and a clean end removes `lab/hunt.json`, so a hunt that was killed or crashed is visible to the guard.

groups.title: The command line
groups.summary: The single entry point: argument parsing, the gates before a command (who plays, the Lie Detector alarm), the wiring of a command's Hunter to the perception service and the player, and the start of every long-lived process. The processes, the lab folder and all 47 commands are listed in this slice's runtime view.

modules.title: The command line
modules.tagline: `python -m gamelab`: 47 subcommands, the safety gates before them, and process glue
modules.summary: The single entry point of gamelab: every process of the autonomous player, from the elevated key player to the perception service, the hunts, the pet feeder and the mini-map, is started as `python -m gamelab <command>`. It checks who plays and whether the Lie Detector alarm is up before anything touches the game, wires a command's Hunter to the perception service and the key player, and turns how a command ended into an exit code.

key_items.name: main
key_items.summary: Parses the line, applies who plays and the Lie Detector gate, runs the command and maps its exceptions to exit codes; always detaches from the perception service.
key_items.details_md: Order: `_play_as` (exit 2 if `--character` comes too late), `_unnamed`, `_refused_as` (exit 2: a non-thief's `lock`, `combo` or `probe run`, `HERS_NOT_YET` saying why), `magic.apply` for `hunt`/`nav`/`tour`, `enable_dpi_awareness`, `client.check_alarm()` for `GAME_COMMANDS` or `args.game`. Exceptions: `client.LieDetectorAlarm` -> 3 with instructions to answer it and run `clear-alarm`; `client.PlayerError`/`RuntimeError` -> 1; a `behavior.safety.HuntStop` -> its `exit_code`; anything else is re-raised. `finally: _close_perception()`.

key_items.name: build_parser
key_items.summary: Declares all 47 subcommands, their options and defaults, and adds `--character` after every command's name.
key_items.details_md: `hunt` takes a mode (`look`, `kill`, `clear`, `shots`); `probe` has its own subparsers (`list`, `run`, `score`), `run` setting `game=True` so the alarm gate applies. `minimap` and `web` share `map_args` (port 8765, host 0.0.0.0). `tour`'s `--grind` (the default since 2026-10-27) and `--camp` are a mutually exclusive group.

key_items.name: _hunter
key_items.signature: def _hunter(args, viewer: bool = False, throws: bool = True, fit=None, restore: bool = True, **kw)
key_items.summary: Builds the Hunter for any command that looks or acts in the game: keys, map, perception client, size fix, eyes, OCR warm-up, phone pushes, published keys, and the start checks of a hunt.
key_items.details_md: Steps: her keys (`keymap.at_start`), the map (`mapdata.load`), `_perception`, then for a command that hunts `_size_fix` + `_fit_start`, the caller's `fit(perception)`, `_eyes`, the OCR warm-up, the `Hunter`, the phone pushes (`notify.BackpackPush`, `Vitals`), `keymap.publish`. `viewer` (`hunt look`): neither sends keys nor tells throws, no size fix, a minimized game waited for. `throws=False` (`pet`, `keys --read`, `stats --read`, `nav --park`): sends keys but doesn't hunt, no size fix, no OCR warm-up. `fit(perception)` runs before the eyes are made (the pet's `PetWait`, `nav --park`'s `_not_minimized`). Commands that take `--low-hp` (`hunt`, `tour`, `probe run`) then wait up to `safety.HP_WAIT_S` (5 s) for her max HP (unless `--low-hp` is a share, 1 or under), collapse her chat box, read her stat window (which shows her max HP too), raise `HpNotRead` if her max HP is still unknown, and raise `TooStrong` on a map whose monsters are too strong for her (both exit 4).

key_items.name: _perception
key_items.signature: def _perception(model, title: str, name: str, acts: bool, throws: bool = False)
key_items.summary: Attaches this command to the perception service as a named client and waits up to PERCEPTION_WAIT_S for its welcome.
key_items.details_md: The client is appended to `_PERCEPTION` so `main` closes it. `ready()` raises `RuntimeError` when another command holds the service on another map. Without a welcome in time the command goes on and its looks stand still until states come.

key_items.name: _record
key_items.summary: Starts the run's telemetry file, claims lab/hunt.json for hunting commands, and writes the run's session record.
key_items.details_md: `telemetry.record_to(command)`; `guard.claim(command)` when `command.split('-')[0]` is in `guard.HUNTS` (`hunt`, `probe`, `nav`, `tour`); `telemetry.emit('session', map, command, mode='live', physics=..., jump_aside, hop_up)`; `gcstats.report_every` (Python's garbage collections once a minute). Called before `_hunter`, whose start may resize the client.

key_items.name: cmd_player
key_items.summary: `player`: runs the key player here, or with `--elevate` relaunches it as administrator through a UAC prompt.
key_items.details_md: `ShellExecuteW(None, 'runas', sys.executable, '-X utf8 -m gamelab player', REPO, SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE)`. A return of 32 or less is an error: 5 the UAC prompt declined, 2 python not found, 3 folder not found. Refused while the alarm is up (`client.check_alarm`).

key_items.name: cmd_perceive
key_items.summary: `perceive`: the perception service's process: one per PC, its telemetry, the rolling recording and the Lie Detector trackers wired in, then `Service.serve`.
key_items.details_md: Takes `service.MUTEX` (or `SAVED_MUTEX` with `--frames`); a second one prints that one is running and returns 0. Live: `telemetry.console_in_background()`, `record_to('perceive')`, a `Publisher`, `Recording(title)` unless `--no-record`, and `Together(LieTracking, VioletaLive)`. With `--frames DIR`: saved PNGs looked at round and round (`--hold` 30 times each), nothing published or recorded, at its own pipe and info file (`GAMELAB_PERCEIVE=saved` reaches it).

key_items.name: cmd_pet
key_items.summary: `pet`: her pet fed by its fullness followed in time; with `--every N` a loop that waits for the game, waits out a wrong-sized client, and runs the guard between follows.
key_items.details_md: Each follow: `_pet_resized` (a client now at another calibrated size ends the process for the babysitter to restart it with eyes for it), `PetWait` (a wrong size, full screen or the game drawn off its client: nothing sent), `_pet_keys` (follows key bindings another command read since), then `hunter.pet.tend(present=...)`. A `PlayerError` (the alarm's limits, no player) is logged and tried again next time. With the alarm up it goes on feeding but never reads (the read double-clicks her).

key_items.name: _guard_pass
key_items.summary: Builds the guard's pass for `pet --every`: the service's newest state, her HP against the stop rule, the phone, and a detached `nav --park --tell`.
key_items.details_md: `latest()` asks the feed for a state no older than `guard.STATE_AGE_S` (3 s) without waiting; `low(st)` compares her HP with `hunter.hp_watch.threshold`; `start_park()` runs `cmd.exe /c set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1&& python -u -X utf8 -m gamelab nav --park --tell >> lab/park.log 2>&1` through `service._start_detached` (WMI), so the park outlives the pet feeder the babysitter stops when it sees it.

key_items.name: _nav_park
key_items.summary: `nav --park`: she goes to the safe place on the map the service looks at, her moves alone; never brings the game forward.
key_items.details_md: Sends nothing if a hunt runs (`guard.running_hunt`), if the game isn't in front (a note for the guard: `retreat.told`), or if no service runs. The map comes from `lab/perceive.json` (`_park_map`), not a `--map` default: at 08:18 on 2026-11-05 a `nav` with none took the service off her map. `--tell` pushes the outcome to the phone.

key_items.name: cmd_tour
key_items.summary: `tour`: the sweep of the map's hunting platforms, or with `--loop` the hunt loop for `--minutes` (grinding by default, `--camp` one ground at a time), then she parks.
key_items.details_md: `--loop --grind` runs `behavior.grind.Grind(tour).run(minutes)`, `--loop --camp` runs `behavior.hunt.Hunt(tour).run(minutes)`, both inside `retreat.on_alarm`, then `park(hunter)`. Without `--loop`, `Tour.run(stops, kinds, kills_per_stop, seconds_per_stop)`.

key_items.name: cmd_clear_alarm
key_items.summary: `clear-alarm`: removes lab/ALARM.json once the Lie Detector's recording has ended; refuses (exit 3) while it is still going.
key_items.details_md: While `lie_recorder.going()` has a folder and the alarm is up, clearing it would let a running player stop `END_S` after the last sight while a person may still be answering it, and the commands run. After clearing, a player that stopped needs `player --elevate` again.

key_items.name: GAME_COMMANDS
key_items.summary: Commands that bring the game to the front or send it input: `main` refuses them (exit 3) while the Lie Detector alarm is up.
key_items.details_md: `probe run` joins them through its parser's `game=True`. Not in it: `pet` (it keeps feeding through the alarm), `perceive`, `watch`, `stop`, and `keys`/`stats`, which check the alarm themselves before `--read` sends anything.

key_items.name: _fit_start
key_items.summary: At a hunting command's start, sets a client of an uncalibrated size right with Alt+Enter twice and waits for it, START_WAIT_S at most.
key_items.details_md: Polls the window every `START_POLL_S` (1 s) without capturing; checks the alarm each round; raises `RuntimeError` after 180 s. It used to wait for ever, while the babysitter kept the pet stopped meanwhile, unfed.

key_items.name: _to_game
key_items.summary: Brings the game to the front before a hunting command's first look and plan, and checks it came (`FRONT_WAIT_S`, 3 s); if not, the command says which window is in front and doesn't start (exit 1).
key_items.details_md: The player refuses every plan while another window is in front, and a look then sees that window: on 2026-10-21 at 01:01:30 a tour's first looks saw another window for 2.5 s and its first plan was refused ("game not in front"). `window.bring_to_front` sends no keys: it attaches to the foreground window's input thread to be allowed `SetForegroundWindow`. Half way through the wait it also switches to the game as Alt+Tab does (`window.SWITCH_FALLBACK`, on; the README says it wasn't tried in game yet).

modules.concurrency: Runs on the main thread of whatever process the command is. It starts other processes: the elevated player through `ShellExecuteW` 'runas' (`cmd_player --elevate`), and, detached through WMI so they outlive it, the perception service (`ServiceClient` -> `service.ensure`, at most every 10 s) and the guard's `nav --park --tell` (`_guard_pass`); `stop` with no hunt runs `nav --park` as a child and waits. Threads come from what it builds: the perception client's `perceive-client` thread, the telemetry writer (`telemetry-writer`; `perceive` adds a `console-writer`), `gcstats`' once-a-minute report (`gc-report`), the OCR warm-up thread of a hunt's start (`ocr-warm`, `perception.messages.warm`), the web server's threads (`minimap`), and the whole service (`perceive`).

decisions.what: `_to_game`: a hunting command brings the game forward and checks it came before its first look and plan.
decisions.why: At 01:01:30 a tour's first looks saw another window for 2.5 s and its first plan was refused ("game not in front").

decisions.what: `_game_geometry` restores a minimized game (commands that act) or waits for it (`watch`, `pet --every`) before reading its size.
decisions.why: Minimized, GetClientRect gave 432x54, not the game's client.

decisions.what: `_minimap_picture` tries 3 times and stops a command whose map has a minimap picture that won't load.
decisions.why: A process where it was None (16:46:50) read her dot with the first map's origin, putting her 640 units off Tree Dungeon for a whole hunt.

decisions.what: Every command's looks come from one perception service; `--feed`/`--no-feed` and `--sweep` removed; `_perception` attaches commands as clients.
decisions.why: The user: "perception should just always run and the other modules just work based on latest perception result"; "run one shared perception process at all times".

decisions.what: `pet --every` with no game window waits for one (`_wait_for_game`, every `GAME_POLL_S`, 5 s) instead of ending.
decisions.why: It ended, and the babysitter started it again every 5 s.

decisions.what: `pet --every` waits out a client that is full screen, another size or drawn off (`behavior.pet.PetWait`) instead of ending.
decisions.why: At 23:21 on 2026-10-25 it ended at once ("not calibrated at 3840x2160 yet") and the babysitter restarted it every 5 s (gamelab/README.md dates `PetWait` from 2026-10-26).

decisions.what: `perceive` keeps the rolling recording from its own frames; `gamelab recorder` is only what runs where it can't.
decisions.why: The user: "The recording should probably just take frames from within the same perception process".

decisions.what: `tour --loop` grinds by default (`--grind`); `--camp` keeps one ground at a time.
decisions.why: The user: "Yes make that the default"; live it made 318-408 EXP a minute on Tree Dungeon on 2026-10-26, camping 283 and 340 on 10-24 and 10-25.

decisions.what: `--low-hp` (`safety_arg`): 1 or under a share of her max HP, over 1 HP; by default her profile's reserve.
decisions.why: Until 2026-10-26 `tour`'s rested her on the chair (30%); until 2026-10-28 it was always a share, 65% by default.

decisions.what: `stats --read --record` catches any exception to say "HER STAT WINDOW MAY BE OPEN IN THE GAME" and write its report before re-raising.
decisions.why: The review of 2026-10-28: a crash after S left the window open, nothing said.

decisions.what: The magician plays `hunt`, `nav` and `tour` (her Magic Claw); `lock`, `combo` and `probe run` stay the thief's.
decisions.why: Her attacks are built for the hunt only (`HERS_NOT_YET` says why for each other command).

decisions.what: `pet --every` tells the pet care the time it waited for the game wasn't the pet's (`hunter.pet.away()`).
decisions.why: At 16:29 that time had been counted, and the pet was fed blind twice.

decisions.what: The run's `session` record carries her physics (`motion.physics.record`).
decisions.why: So a recorded run says how it planned her moves.

decisions.what: `stop` stops a hunt and parks her (`stop-player` stops the player); `nav --park` takes its map from the service's info file; the guard runs inside `pet --every`.
decisions.why: A grind killed with Stop-Process left her among monsters until she died; and at 08:18 a `nav` with no `--map` took the service off her map.

gotchas: `stop` stops the running hunt and parks her; `stop-player` stops the key player. They used to be easy to confuse.
A hunt killed or crashed (exit 1 included) leaves `lab/hunt.json` behind: the guard takes that as "ended without parking her" and parks her.
While `lab/ALARM.json` is up even `hunt look`, `snap` and `calibrate` are refused (they are in `GAME_COMMANDS`), but `pet --every` keeps feeding and `perceive` keeps running.
`--character` must come before her physics is loaded (`_play_as`); under `character use` alone, an in-game command other than `perceive`, `pet` and the hunting commands plays the thief and says so.
A hunting command is refused at its start if another hunting command holds the service on another map; viewers on another map see the held map's places (they say so).
`window 1366x768` resizes through the player (a normal program can't resize the admin window); `window --recover` instead switches full screen and back with Alt+Enter twice.
`minimap` falls back to the window alone if port 8765 is taken; `web` then exits 1.
`watch --hz` does nothing now: the service's rate is its own (15 a second).
`probe score --line` sets `reach.LINE` for that process only; `coverage --ways` and `nav/tour --ways` set `route.ROUTES` the same way (`_ways`).
`pet --every` ends with exit 0 when the client changes to another calibrated size: by design, for the babysitter to restart it with eyes for that size.

`save-recent --png`'s help still says the saves keep 5 GB; the code keeps 20 GB (`rolling.RECENT_KEEP_BYTES`, raised on 2026-10-29).

flows.title: A hunt's start, from the command line to its first key
flows.summary: What `python -m gamelab tour --loop` does before she moves: the gates, the telemetry, attaching to perception, fixing the window and checking her HP, then the hunt loop inside the Lie Detector's retreat.
flows.trigger: A person types `python -m gamelab tour --loop --minutes 20 --map 10002073` (the player and the service already running)

steps.text: Parses the line; `_play_as` sets `GAMELAB_CHARACTER` before her physics loads; `_refused_as` lets any character hunt; `magic.apply` switches to Magic Claw for the magician; `client.check_alarm()` exits 3 if `lab/ALARM.json` is up. Then it calls `cmd_tour`.
`cmd_tour` first records the run: opens `lab/telemetry/<time>-tour.jsonl`, writes `lab/hunt.json` (`guard.claim`) and the `session` record with her physics.
Builds the agent: her keys from the bindings last read (else config.toml), the map's data, then the steps below in this order.

A `ServiceClient` says hello over the pipe (acts, throws, the map); if no service answers, the client starts one through WMI; it waits up to 20 s for the welcome and stops if the service perceives another character.
A client at a size the eyes have no calibration for is set right with Alt+Enter twice (`control.window_size.SizeFix`), waited for 180 s at most.

Eyes on the service's frames (never a capture of their own) with the map's monster detector and its minimap picture (3 tries; a map whose picture won't load stops the command). Then the OCR warms on a thread, the Hunter is built, the phone pushes are wired, and her keys go to `lab/alarm_keys.json` for the player's Lie Detector allowance.

Waits up to 5 s for her max HP off the HUD; then her chat box is collapsed (`collapse_chat`), her stat window read (`read_stats`), and a map whose monsters are too strong for her refused (`too_strong`).
Back in `cmd_tour`: a fighting navigator is made, then the game is brought to the front and waited for 3 s; the player refuses plans while another window is in front.
Wraps the hunt: on the Lie Detector or a hunt stop she goes to a safe place before the exception reaches `main`.
The hunt loop for `--minutes`: a decision after every look of the service's latest state; its keys go out as plans through `control.client`.
Time's up: she parks on the map's safe place instead of being left among the monsters.
At the end: `_hunt_over` removes `lab/hunt.json` on a clean end, and `_close_perception` detaches from the service and prints how many states it was handed.

flows.title: A key plan's round trip through the lab folder
flows.summary: How a normal process gets keys into the admin game window: a JSON file in the inbox, claimed by renaming, played, answered in the outbox.
flows.trigger: Any command that acts calls `client.submit` or `client.send` + `client.wait`

steps.text: Refuses with the alarm up unless the plan has one of the four kinds; writes `inbox/<id>.tmp` and renames it to `<id>.json` so the player never reads half a plan.
Every 10 ms takes the first `*.json` in name order (none before the watchdog's first look) and renames it to `.running`: from then on the client can cancel it but no longer withdraw it.

Refuses it during an alarm unless its kind allows it, validates it (any key config.toml can name, at most 400 events, 20 s and 900 frames), brings the game forward if asked, presses the events on a `key-player` thread, records frames (saved to `outbox/<id>.npz`), and stops at once on `<id>.cancel` or the Lie Detector.
Removes the `.running` file and writes the result to `outbox/<id>.tmp`, renamed to `<id>.json` so the client never reads half a result.

Polls every 10 ms; withdraws a plan not yet taken if the alarm goes up; after 120 s says the player may not be running. Reads the result (retrying about 1 s while Windows holds it locked), deletes it and any leftover cancel file, and raises `LieDetectorAlarm` or `PlayerError` on an error.

flows.title: Between hunts: the pet feeder's guard parks her
flows.summary: With no hunt running, the babysitter's `pet --every 1` feeds her pet and runs the guard each second; when she is in trouble the guard starts a detached `nav --park`.
flows.trigger: The babysitter starts `pet --every 1 --map M` because no hunting command's process is running

steps.text: Waits for the game window if there is none, says a park wanted while the game is minimized, builds the Hunter (keys but no throws, `PetWait` for a wrong-sized client) and the guard's pass.
Between follows of the pet's fullness, runs a guard pass every `GUARD_S` (1 s); a pass that fails is logged once a kind and never stops the pet's care.

Reads `lab/guard_mode.txt`, turns a dead hunt's `lab/hunt.json` into `lab/park_note.json`, and looks at the service's newest state: two touches within 30 s, HP under the stop rule on two passes, or a note set it off.

Dead: one push. Alarm up: no moves. Played by hand: left alone. Game in front and player up: start a park (again at most every 2 minutes, 3 times an episode). Else a push, and she parks at the game's return.
`start_park` launches `nav --park --tell` detached through WMI, its console appended to `lab/park.log`; the babysitter, seeing a `nav` process, stops the pet feeder meanwhile.

Sends nothing if a hunt runs, the game isn't in front or no service runs; takes the map from `lab/perceive.json`; drives her moves alone to the safe place (`retreat.park`), and pushes the outcome to the phone.
Writes how it came out to `lab/parked.json` (or a note in `lab/park_note.json` if she isn't there), which `gamelab stop` and the guard read.

flows.title: The Lie Detector, across the processes
flows.summary: One sighting by the elevated player's watchdog changes what every other process may do, through one file.
flows.trigger: The game shows a Lie Detector form while a hunt and the pet feeder run

steps.text: Looks 4 times a second; on a sighting the alarm Event is set first (input stops within about 10 ms, held keys let go), then `control.alarm.raise_alarm` writes `lab/ALARM.json`, saves a screenshot and pages the PC; the cycle is recorded.
The hunt's running plan is answered with the Lie Detector error and raises `LieDetectorAlarm`; any new plan without a kind is refused before it is written.
Moves her to a safe place within 10 s with plans of kind `retreat` (her arrows, jump, up, down), which the player takes for 12 s after the sighting.
Catches `LieDetectorAlarm`, removes `lab/hunt.json`, prints what to do, exits 3.

The service sees `ALARM.json`: its mini-game tracker (a child process) follows the target and moves the cursor through the player (`lie_cursor`); the Violetta watcher clicks the answer and the pass's OK (`lie_ok`).
Keeps feeding by the fullness it follows (`pet_food`, 3 a minute at most) and reads nothing until the alarm is cleared.
The rolling recording saves the 5 minutes before into the cycle's folder (`before/`) and the alarm's clip to `lab/alarm_clips/`.

A person answers it, then `clear-alarm` removes `ALARM.json` (refused, exit 3, while the recording is still going). A cycle with no Truth Booth clears itself (`player.AUTO_RESUME`); after one with it, the player stops and needs `player --elevate` again.

not_done: The babysitter is outside the repo (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/babysit3.ps1`, its owner's to change): its rules exist only in its own header and the README's notes, and it finds processes by regexes over their command lines.

Who plays isn't read off the game (her bottom bar, the design's S0g): `character check` reads nothing yet, and a non-thief must be named for in-game commands other than `perceive`, `pet` and the hunting commands.

The perception service doesn't restart itself: after a crash or its watchdog's exit, perception stops until a client's `ensure` (at most every 10 s) or the babysitter starts another. A hang that holds Python's lock stops its watchdog thread too (README: not seen).
The rolling recording lives in the service's memory: a service restart loses its last 5 minutes.
The guard is blind with the game behind another window or minimized, and on any map but the babysitter's fixed `pet --map`; there `stop` with no hunt can't park her.
"Played by hand" can't be told for certain; Chrome Remote Desktop's injected keys should count, read off the process list but not tried.
`gamelab stop`'s cancel files should cut plans already sent (a pick-up or Lucky Seven tap in the simulator came from plans sent before it): not tried live.
`lock`, `combo` and `probe run` are the thief's only (`HERS_NOT_YET`).
The external grind loops' STOP file is a hard-coded path outside the repo (`behavior.guard.LOOP_STOP`).

processes.name: The key player
processes.lifetime: Started by a person (`player --elevate`: the UAC prompt needs their click). Runs until `lab/STOP` appears (`stop-player`), after 24 idle hours (`IDLE_LIMIT_S`; not while it records a Lie Detector), if its Lie Detector watch thread dies, or after a Lie Detector whose cycle saw the Truth Booth, once a person has cleared the alarm and the game has shown none for `END_S` (10 s). An answered Lie Detector with no Truth Booth clears its own alarm and the player carries on (`AUTO_RESUME`, since 2026-10-29). It refuses to start while the alarm is up.
processes.summary: The only process with administrator rights: MapleStory runs elevated, and Windows blocks input from normal programs into admin windows. It plays JSON plans from `lab/inbox` (keys, mouse moves and clicks inside the game window, resizes), only while the game is in front, records the client area when asked, and answers in `lab/outbox`. A watchdog looks for the Lie Detector 4 times a second and stops all input within about 10 ms.
processes.details_md:
**How it starts.** `cmd_player --elevate` calls `ShellExecuteW('runas', python, '-X utf8 -m gamelab player')`, minimized and not activated (`SW_SHOWMINNOACTIVE`); the elevated copy runs `control.player.serve()`. It deletes leftover inbox files, writes `lab/player.json` (`{splice, pid, started}`: clients check it before splicing plans), starts the watchdog and takes no plan before the watchdog's first look.

**What keeps it safe** (gamelab/README.md, How the keys get to the game): it runs no code from plans; it presses any key config.toml can name and both mouse buttons, moves the pointer only inside the game window, and only with the game in front; its code and key list are loaded once at start, and it loads as little of gamelab as it can (a test enforces this). A plan is limited to 400 events, 20 s and 900 frames.

**With the alarm up** it refuses every plan but four kinds: `pet_food` (one tap, 3 a minute), `retreat` (her moves only, for 12 s after the sighting), `lie_cursor` (one move inside the mini-game's board, or one click on a Violetta answer button) and `lie_ok` (one click on the pass's OK). It writes `lab/ALARM.json` first, then a screenshot, pages the PC (sounds and a Windows notification that doesn't take focus) and pushes to the phone if `lab/bark.json` or `lab/smtp.json` are set up. Its log, `lab/player.log`, rotates past 5 MB when it starts.
threads: the serve loop (main thread): the inbox looked at every 10 ms, one plan at a time

`lie-detector-watch` (Watchdog): a look at the game every 0.25 s whether or not a plan runs; while a cycle is recorded, `lie-detector-recording` writes its index and `lie-detector-prune` keeps the folder to 10 GB
`key-player`: a thread per plan that presses its events on time
phone pushes (`bark-push`, `text-mail`), and a hidden PowerShell process for each Windows notification

processes.name: The perception service
processes.lifetime: Meant to run at all times, one per PC (the named mutex `Local\gamelab-perceive`; a second prints that one runs and exits 0). Started by the babysitter, or by any command's client that can't reach one (`service.ensure`: detached through WMI, at most every 10 s, its console in `lab/perceive.log`). Ends on Ctrl+C or `--minutes`, or ends itself (exit 3) when its frame loop hasn't gone round for 10 s (`STUCK_S`; 60 s while a run is built) so that another can be started.
processes.summary: Looks at the game 15 times a second and hands the newest state (her place, the HUD, every monster with its track, the drops) to every command that attaches; no command captures the screen itself. It publishes what it sees as telemetry for the mini-map, keeps the rolling 5-minute recording, and while the Lie Detector alarm is up follows the mini-game's target and the Violetta game.
processes.details_md:
**Why it exists.** Until 2026-10-25 every command that looked had a feed child process of its own (spawn, below-normal priority, a ring of 4 frames in shared memory) and a desktop duplication of its own; with `watch`, the pet and a hunt that was three feeds at 1.33-1.50 cores each and the duplications ran out. Now one process: measured offline on saved frames at its paces then (10 frames a second idle, 26.5 hunting), 0.55 cores with only a viewer and 1.66 with a hunting client (gamelab/README.md, The perception service); it runs at 15 a second for everyone now. It runs at normal priority with OpenCV on one thread and 1 ms timers (`service.settle`).

**Its clients.** Each command's `ServiceClient` connects to `\\.\pipe\gamelab-perceive` with the authkey from `lab/perceive.json`, says `hello`, and then sends `ask` (what to search on the next frame), `throw`, `full` (the next frame at full size), `status`, `bye`. States go down the pipe pickled once, by a writer thread per client that keeps the newest 64 (`QUEUE_KEEP`; older ones dropped and counted as a gap); frames are read from shared-memory rings (16 look frames, 2 full-size). A client that hears nothing for 10 s reconnects; one that can't reach a service starts one. A command that hunts holds the map; a second hunting command on another map is refused.

**What else runs in it.** Telemetry in `lab/telemetry/<time>-perceive.jsonl` (a scene 10 times a second, tracks twice, events, a `perf` record every 10 s); the rolling recording (`control.recording`, 15 frames a second, the last 5 minutes in memory, saves written by a part-writer child); and, while the alarm is up, `LieTracking` (its tracker in a child process) and `VioletaLive` (a YOLO model on the GPU). Those two move the cursor and click through the player; the service itself never presses a key or brings the game forward.

**Saved frames.** `perceive --frames DIR` runs the same loop on PNGs, offline, at its own pipe, mutex and `lab/perceive-saved.json`; commands reach it with `GAMELAB_PERCEIVE=saved`.

processes.summary: A PowerShell script outside the repo that keeps the always-on processes up: it starts the perception service when none runs, stops the pet feeder while a hunting command's process runs and starts it again after, and hands the rolling recording over from an old `gamelab recorder` to the service.
processes.details_md: What the repo says of it (gamelab/README.md): it matches processes by their command lines (the README's snippet of its predecessor uses `gamelab perceive(?!.*--frames)` and `gamelab (tour|hunt|nav|probe|combo|act|do) `), which is why every subcommand also takes `--character` after its name and why the guard parks through a separate `nav` process. It starts programs detached through WMI with `D:\MapleHelper` as their folder. It stops the old recorder only once that one has nothing left to write (no alarm up or begun in the last 5 minutes, no save asked or waiting), and starts it when no recording runs. Its idle guard moves a python whose command line has `spawn_main(parent_pid` to Idle priority within 5 s. It starts the pet feeder with a fixed `--map` (10002073 when the guard section was written), so the guard is blind on other maps. Whether it runs as administrator isn't recorded in the repo.

processes.name: The mini-map and web page
processes.command: python -m gamelab minimap   (or: python -m gamelab web)
processes.lifetime: Started by a person; until the window is closed or Ctrl+C (`web`).
processes.summary: Reads telemetry only and never touches the game: a tkinter window placed beside the game (never over it, since captures see what is on top), and a standard-library HTTP server on port 8765 that pushes the run's records to a phone as Server-Sent Events. The same server serves the review pages and `/tls/`.
processes.details_md: `cmd_minimap` builds the source (`LiveSource` follows the newest run and the perception service's file; `--replay FILE`; `--plan SRC DST`), starts `ui.web` (a `Feed` thread and the server's threads) unless `--window-only`, then runs `MapWindow` on the main thread. `_beside_game` places the window right of, left of or below the game's client on a monitor. Anyone who reaches the address can watch; a Cloudflare tunnel (outside gamelab) can expose it, with `/tls/` behind a Cloudflare Access login.
threads: the tkinter main loop (the window)
`web`: the HTTP server (a thread per request or stream)
`telemetry`: the web Feed reading the run's records

talks_to.what: what the command planned and did
what is on screen

processes.name: The mini-game tracker
processes.lifetime: A child of the perception service: started when the Lie Detector alarm goes up, stopped 60 s after it has gone (`CHILD_IDLE_S`).
processes.summary: Follows the Lie Detector mini-game's target on the service's frames, in a process of its own so it neither shares the frame loop's Python lock nor its one OpenCV thread. Each round's answers go to `lab/lie_target/<time>.jsonl`; the service moves the cursor through the player.
processes.details_md: Below-normal priority, no window, OpenCV on 6 threads (`CHILD_THREADS`): in the service a frame took 78 ms against 52-64 here, over the 66 ms of 15 frames a second. The board's pictures go down its stdin one when it is ready; behind, it takes the newest.
threads: its tracker's OpenCV threads

talks_to.what: board pictures down, the target's position up

processes.name: The part writer
processes.lifetime: A child of the perception service, one per save of the rolling recording (an alarm's `before/` and clip, `save-recent`); ends once the part is written (600 s at most).
processes.summary: Decodes and encodes a saved stretch of the rolling recording to JPEG or PNG in a process of its own, so a save doesn't hold up the service's frame loop. If it can't start or fails, the service writes the part itself.
processes.details_md: Written inside the service, a 120 s save made the frame loop's steps wait 18-21 ms against 1-2 and dropped it to 8.4-9.7 frames a second; written apart, 3-4 ms (`rolling.write_part_apart`). It runs below normal (Idle if its parent is), its threads at the lowest priority.
threads: its encoder threads (4, or 2 while a command hunts)

talks_to.what: the frames in, the part's summary out

processes.name: The old rolling recorder
processes.lifetime: Only where the service doesn't record (a service of older code, down, or `perceive --no-record`): the babysitter starts it then, and stops it once the service waits for the recorders' mutex and it has nothing left to write.
processes.summary: The rolling recording as it ran until 2026-10-26: its own mss capture of the game window 10 times a second, the last 5 minutes kept in memory, saved on a Lie Detector alarm and by `save-recent`. One recorder at a time on the PC, this or the service's.
processes.details_md: Below-normal priority (`rolling.quiet`). It answers `save-recent` through `lab/recorder/inbox` and `outbox` and writes `lab/recorder/status.json` every 5 s (`recorder --status` reads it).
threads: the ticks (main), `rolling-saves`

talks_to.what: who records
`save-recent` and `recorder --status`

processes.name: Short commands and viewers
processes.command: python -m gamelab stop | stop-player | clear-alarm | guard | save-recent | watch | hunt look | map | ...
processes.lifetime: Started by a person (or by Claude driving gamelab); each runs once and ends, but `watch` until Ctrl+C or `--minutes`.
processes.summary: The commands that steer or watch the long-lived processes: `stop` (a hunt stops and she parks), `stop-player`, `clear-alarm`, `guard`, `save-recent`, the viewers `watch`, `hunt look` and `map` (clients of the service that send nothing), and the offline tools (simulator, benches, analyses) that never touch the game.
processes.details_md: `stop` writes `lab/stop_hunt.json` for the running hunt, cuts the player's running plans with cancel files, touches the external grind loop's STOP file, and waits up to 300 s to say where she parked (`lab/parked.json`); with no hunt it runs `nav --park` itself. `stop-player` touches `lab/STOP` and waits 10 s for the player's log to say it stopped.
